 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. American tennis player Ben Shelton will be switching from On to New Balance in 2027.
 The rumors of Shelton leaving On have been rampant for months, but the choice of New Balance was somewhat of a surprise. Shelton wore New Balance earlier in his career. All the major brands courted the top-ranked American ATP player.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Media reports revealed Shelton's compensation . He will receive $5 million a year of fixed pay for wearing New Balance, Incentives up to $8 million are available. That includes $5 million if he ends the year ranked in the ATP Top 10 and $3 million if he finishes the year as ATP World No. 1.
 MORE: Ben Shelton, Trinity Rodman competing for biggest titles of their careers this week 
 Is he getting more money than Gauff?
 Coco Gauff defeated Marta Kostyuk, earning a chance to advance in the WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
 The short answer appears to be yes based on publicly known information. Gauff, 22, has endorsed New Balance since she was 14. Her most recent contract extension occurred in 2022. Terms of her 2022 deal are undisclosed, though it is believed she earns $1 million per year. Incentives are likely built into her deal.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Gauff also got a signature shoe, the Coco CG1, and has an agreement through New Balance to work with Miu Miu, an Italian brand. Shelton will also get a signature shoe out of his deal.
 If Gauff's deal is up for renewal in 2027, the three-time Grand Slam champion (twice in singles and once in doubles) and 2024 WTA Finals champion, may want to renegotiate to get Shelton-like compensation.
 MORE: Coco Gauff matches Serena Williams feat with legacy-building win in US Open Round of 16 
 Why is Shelton's deal the only one revealed?
 Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen , Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Shohei Ohtani and Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg are also New Balance athletes. Contract terms remain undisclosed. That means we have no basis of comparison.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Shelton's American ATP compatriot Tommy Paul is also a New Balance athlete since 2021, but the terms of his deal are also unknown.
